target_customer: System administrators and developers running servers across multiple cloud providers
problem: Monitoring and managing servers spread across several cloud providers needed one dashboard instead of separate tools per provider.
business_model: SaaS subscription for server monitoring and management

founders.name: Logan Welliver
education: Oregon State University, graphic design degree
founders.background_notes: Oregon State University article says he had the graphic design degree and made the product visually intuitive. The YC page lists him as the only founder.

founders.name: Alex Polvi
founders.background_notes: Named in Oregon State and Xconomy coverage as a founder of Cloudkick and OSU graduate; not listed on the YC page opened, so role listed from press sources only.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents and APIs across many cloud providers with metrics collection and alerting, built by a small student team.

defensibility.rationale: Agent deployment creates some switching cost, but monitoring was a crowded field and the clouds themselves could add monitoring.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rackspace bought Cloudkick in December 2010 and later replaced it with its own Cloud Monitoring product, disabling all accounts on 2013-05-31.

market_need_then: Multiple public clouds including EC2, GoGrid, Linode and Rackspace were in use by 2009 and Cloudkick supported several of them. A 2010 article argued it was the only company focused solely on cloud performance monitoring.

branding.domain_note: Used cloudkick.com; no purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: Design led by the cofounder with a graphic design degree, per Oregon State coverage.

branding.community_and_virality: No community or merch evidence found. Rackspace said it would keep using the Cloudkick brand after the acquisition.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in a sysadmin niche for about two years; no sourced evidence of the brand driving growth.

pivots.from: Scholarship idea described as Kiva.org for scholarships

outcome_analysis: Cloudkick started in early 2009 from a university team after an earlier scholarship idea, joined YC W09, raised roughly 2.75 million dollars across two rounds in aggregator data, and was sold to Rackspace on 2010-12-16 with undisclosed terms and 12 employees joining. Rackspace kept the brand briefly but later replaced the product with its own monitoring service and disabled accounts in May 2013. The exit came about two years after founding, which fits a fast acqui-style outcome tied to multi-cloud tailwinds.
notes: Round figures come from aggregators (Seedtable, CB Insights) and one press report of about $3M; no company announcement was opened, so treat amounts as unverified aggregator data. CB Insights also lists a January 2009 seed of unknown amount and a total of $2.77M. The Rackspace price was undisclosed. Competitor source dates were not visible; the RightScale comparison article date is unknown. The account disablement date of 2013-05-31 is from a search summary. Founder prior employers not found. The cloudkick.com fetch returned 503. Name origin not found. RightScale and Tap In Systems appear in an undated Network World comparison and a 2010 article, so they are not listed as dated competitors.
